program.checker_template:
Execute ONE saved check. Return status, evidence, confidence (0 to 1 or null), and used_dependency_ids. You receive no reference label or optimizer feedback. Do not predict what the optimizer wants.
Support checks receive source and edited images. Inspect only the saved visual proposition and binding. When dependencies are supplied, use those ancestor observations as context and investigate the more specific proposition yourself; do not simply repeat the parent answer. Use pass/fail/unknown. A pass on a broad parent does not imply a nested check passes. Known negative evidence is usable; uncertain or missing evidence is unknown. Do not award requested completion credit to supporting facts.
The requested fulfillment readout receives NO images. Use ALL and ONLY saved support observations, the original instruction, rubric and saved composition criteria. Use complete/partial/absent/unknown. Mere texture or object presence must not silently establish whole-image conversion or a requested spatial relation. Known progress plus evidenced incompleteness may be partial; absence means no requested progress. Missing necessary evidence is unknown, never a fabricated failure or completion. Do not infer new visual facts.
used_dependency_ids must name every supplied dependency check_id exactly once in saved order (empty when none). Confidence is self-report, not calibrated correctness.

The two valid, queried checks independently report fail with strong confidence, and the aggregate correctly labels no, so do not alter the criterion to force a different label. Preserve the existing pass/fail/unknown routing and partial-progress logic: distinguish actual movement toward the requested placement from unrelated edits, and retain unknown when evidence is insufficient. rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The support checks do not reliably distinguish the requested flower from other flowers. s1 assesses the book and “the flower,” while s3 permits either of two flowers to establish the relation; s2 likewise treats progress toward the singular requested relation without identifying which flower is the target. Thus a different flower could satisfy the endpoint or progress checks, and the fulfillment readout could incorrectly award completion or partial credit. The program otherwise preserves the requested relation and rubric, but this target ambiguity makes its evidence insufficient.

The support checks do not provide a sound, non-overlapping basis for the fulfillment readout. s1 can pass when the book is already behind the flower, without establishing that the requested move occurred; s3 can establish progress by comparing source and edit, but its criteria do not establish whether the final placement is complete. The readout nevertheless treats s1 passing as sufficient for completion, so it can award yes without evidence that the requested change happened. Also, s2 is nested under s3 but asks about progress from the edited image alone, which cannot reliably distinguish a changed placement from one that was already present. The composition therefore risks both unsupported completion and unsupported progress.

The fulfillment rule is contradictory and overstates what its supports establish. s1 only checks whether the book is behind a flower in the edited image; it does not establish that this is the same rose shown in the source, yet fulfillment requires that identity. Also, s3 can pass for movement toward the source rose without establishing that the book is still incompletely placed, while the rule awards partial on s3 pass whenever completion is not established. Thus it can label a completed placement partial when s1 is unknown, or infer progress without evidence that the requested placement remains incomplete. The supports do not compose the requested completion/progress distinction reliably.

transaction.reason: Add a nested, image-grounded check for the requested behind relation beyond obvious occlusion. The edited image has a book and two flowers, so the check must not let either newly appearing flower substitute for the source rose; it should assess whether any visible depth cue establishes the book behind the source rose. Keep the existing source-to-edit progress check and readout composition intact, with unknown where identity or depth cannot be determined.

actions.question: In the edited image, is the book visibly behind the same rose shown in the source image, based on a clear depth or placement cue even if they do not overlap?
actions.criteria: Pass only if the edited image provides a clear visual cue that the book is behind the source rose; mere left-right separation or the presence of other flowers is not sufficient. Fail if the image clearly establishes that the book is not behind the source rose. Unknown if the rose's identity or the relative depth cannot be determined.
actions.binding: Compare the source rose with the edited image and assess only the book's relation to that same rose. Do not treat either additional flower as the requested rose, and do not infer depth from left-right ordering alone.

rejected_diagnostics.semantic_rejection: The fulfillment composition is contradictory and does not faithfully implement the rubric. It requires both s1 and s3 to pass for completion, but s1 is a broad check of the same relation and s3 is a nested, more specific check; a broad pass must not be treated as a separate necessary condition. More importantly, it says a fail from either rules out completion, while s1 can fail on evidence that the more specific s3 could resolve differently. The partial rule also requires s2 to pass and completion to be ruled out by clear evidence, but does not specify how to compose conflicting or unknown support results consistently. The program therefore risks turning unresolved or coarse evidence into a negative completion judgment instead of leaving it unknown.

The program adds an unsupported requirement to inspect both flowers and treats separation from both as evidence of no progress. The instruction refers to a flower, not necessarily two, and a book may have progressed toward the requested placement without visible overlap yet. Thus s3 can incorrectly block valid progress evidence from s2, causing the fulfillment readout to report absent instead of partial. The original single-object relation and extent are otherwise represented, but this composition rule is not semantically safe.
